attribution.note: Marcus states this in his own voice and endorses it.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves an observation about growing evidence of data constraints in the surrounding discussion of LLM scaling.

contract.note: The ordinary contextual reading concerns emerging constraints on usable training data. Assessing contemporaneous evidence of those constraints is fair; requiring proof of complete exhaustion would overstate the claim.

evidence.note: The June 2024 research estimates finite usable public-text supply and projects scaling demand overtaking it. It supports evidence of a prospective constraint, not present exhaustion.
The July 2024 longitudinal audit documents increasing access restrictions, supporting practical constraints on usable supply if restrictions are respected or enforced.

The April 2024 experiments show that accumulating real and synthetic data can prevent collapse. This qualifies the shortage argument but does not establish enough useful data for sustained frontier scaling.

reviews.rationale: Research available by publication supplied both a quantified prospective limit on usable human-generated text and evidence of growing access restrictions, meeting the contract. Synthetic-data results qualify the implications but do not negate the existence of growing evidence of constraints. Present exhaustion or an inevitable halt is not established or required.
